brief: TME argues the recent market rotation redistributed risk rather than diversifying it: retail crowding into the Magnificent Seven, institutional crowding into AI infrastructure, and defensive flows into dividend shares all share exposure to the cost of capital. From September 10 to 16, retail sold technology funds and most individual stocks but bought about $1.6 billion of Magnificent Seven stocks, implying roughly $2.2 billion of selling outside that group. GS reads falling SPX breadth (share of members above their 50-day average) beneath a resilient headline index as a correction, not yet a structural breakdown. GS/JPM data show retail favors Nvidia and large platforms while prime brokerage positioning concentrates further down the AI supply chain, near crowding extremes in analog semis, data centers and defense. Mag7 hyperscaler capex reached about $165 billion in Q2, up roughly 89% year over year, with estimates near $733 billion for 2026 and above $1 trillion by 2028. BTIG cites chip-equipment lead times stretching to 10 months and lasers to 40 months. Because AI buildout is increasingly debt-financed, TME warns rising rates could hit AI and dividend shares together, and proposes a 10-year payer spread or TLT put spread sized as insurance, not a directional short.
